problem:
Which of the following affine transformations are invertible?

- ${T}_{1}:[\begin{aligned}u \\ v\end{aligned}]⟶[\begin{aligned}6u+3v+3 \\ 10u+5v\end{aligned}]$
- ${T}_{2}:[\begin{aligned}u \\ v\end{aligned}]⟶[\begin{aligned}1-3u-4v \\ 3u+4v-2\end{aligned}]$
- ${T}_{3}:[\begin{aligned}u \\ v\end{aligned}]⟶[\begin{aligned}4-6u-4v \\ 8u+7v-7\end{aligned}]$
worked_solution:
An affine transformation $T:{R}^{2}\to {R}^{2}$ is a function of the form

$$
x=Au+b,
$$

where $x,u,$ and $b$ are column vectors in ${R}^{2},$ and $A$ is a $2\times 2$ matrix.

The transformation is invertible if the matrix $A$ is invertible. That is, if $det(A)\ne 0.$

With this in mind, let's look at each transformation in turn.

- Transformation ${T}_{1}$ is not invertible. Notice that ${T}_{1}$ can be expressed as

$$
\begin{aligned}[\begin{aligned}x \\ y\end{aligned}] & =[\begin{aligned}6u+3v+3 \\ 10u+5v\end{aligned}] \\  & =[\begin{aligned}6u+3v \\ 10u+5v\end{aligned}]+[\begin{aligned}3 \\ 0\end{aligned}] \\  & ={{[\begin{aligned}6 & 3 \\ 10 & 5\end{aligned}]}_{⏟}}_{A}\cdot {{[\begin{aligned}u \\ v\end{aligned}]}_{⏟}}_{u}+{{[\begin{aligned}3 \\ 0\end{aligned}]}_{⏟}}_{b}.\end{aligned}
$$

Computing the determinant of $A,$ we get

$$
det(A)=|\begin{aligned}6 & 3 \\ 10 & 5\end{aligned}|=5\cdot 6-3\cdot 10=0.
$$

Since the determinant is zero, ${T}_{1}$ is *not* invertible.

- Transformation ${T}_{2}$ is not invertible. Notice that ${T}_{2}$ can be expressed as

$$
\begin{aligned}[\begin{aligned}x \\ y\end{aligned}] & =[\begin{aligned}1-3u-4v \\ 3u+4v-2\end{aligned}] \\  & =[\begin{aligned}-3u-4v \\ 3u+4v\end{aligned}]+[\begin{aligned}1 \\ -2\end{aligned}] \\  & ={{[\begin{aligned}-3 & -4 \\ 3 & 4\end{aligned}]}_{⏟}}_{A}\cdot {{[\begin{aligned}u \\ v\end{aligned}]}_{⏟}}_{u}+{{[\begin{aligned}1 \\ -2\end{aligned}]}_{⏟}}_{b}.\end{aligned}
$$

Computing the determinant of $A,$ we get

$$
det(A)=|\begin{aligned}-3 & -4 \\ 3 & 4\end{aligned}|=4\cdot (-3)-(-4)\cdot 3=0.
$$

Since the determinant is zero, ${T}_{2}$ is *not* invertible.

- Transformation ${T}_{3}$ is invertible. Notice that ${T}_{3}$ can be expressed as

$$
\begin{aligned}[\begin{aligned}x \\ y\end{aligned}] & =[\begin{aligned}4-6u-4v \\ 8u+7v-7\end{aligned}] \\  & =[\begin{aligned}-6u-4v \\ 8u+7v\end{aligned}]+[\begin{aligned}4 \\ -7\end{aligned}] \\  & ={{[\begin{aligned}-6 & -4 \\ 8 & 7\end{aligned}]}_{⏟}}_{A}\cdot {{[\begin{aligned}u \\ v\end{aligned}]}_{⏟}}_{u}+{{[\begin{aligned}4 \\ -7\end{aligned}]}_{⏟}}_{b}.\end{aligned}
$$

Computing the determinant of $A,$ we get

$$
det(A)=|\begin{aligned}-6 & -4 \\ 8 & 7\end{aligned}|=7\cdot (-6)-(-4)\cdot 8=-10\ne 0.
$$

Since the determinant is nonzero, ${T}_{3}$ is invertible.

Therefore, the correct answer is "${T}_{3}$ only."
